source_text: 1. Ostenso manifeste, quod in principio Verbum exsistens apud Deum, per quem omnia facta sunt, qui et semper aderat generi humano, hune in novissimis temporibus secundum prefinitum tempus a Patre, unitum suo plasmati, passibilem hominem factum, exclusa est omnis contradictio dicentium: Si ergo tune natus est, non erat ergo ante Christus. Ostendimus enim, quia non tune ccepit Filius Dei, exsistens semper apud Patrem; sed quando incarnatus est, et homo factus, longam hominum expositionem in seipso recapitulavit, in compendio nobis salutem prestans, ut quod perdideramus in Adam, id est, secundum imaginem et similitudinem esse Dei, hoc in Christo Jesu reciperemus. 2. Quia enim non erat possibile, eum hominem qui semel victus fuerat et elisus per inobedientiam, replasmare, et obtinere Sbravium victoria, iterum autem impossibile erat ut salutem perciperet qui sub peccato ceciderat, utraque operatus est Filius, Verbum Dei exsistens, a Patre descendens, et incarnatus, et usque ad mortem descendens, et dispensationem consummans salutis nostre, cui credere nos indubitate adhortans, iterum ®dicit: Ne dixeris in corde tuo, Quis ascendit in celum? hoc est Christum deducere. Aut, Quis descendit in abyssum? hoe est Christum a mortuis liberare; deinde infert: Quoniam si confitearis in ore tuo Dominum Jesum, et credideris in corde tuo, quoniam Deus illum excitavit a mortuis, salvous eris. Et rationem reddidit propter quam causam hee fecit Verbum Dei, dicens: Jn hoc enim * Christus et vixit, et mortwus est, et resurrexit, ut vivorum et mortuorum dominetur. Et iterum ad Corinthios scribens ait : Vos autem annuntiamus Christum * Jesum crucifizum. Et infert: Oalix benedictionis quem benedicimus, nonne communicatio sanguinis est Christi? Quis est autem qui communicavit nobis de escis? Utrum is qui ab illis affingitur sursum Christus, superextensus Horo, id est fini, et formavit eorum matrem: an VETO qui ex virgine est Emmanuel, qui butyrum et mel manduCavit, de quo ait propheta: Et homo est, et quis cognoscet eum? Hic idem a Paulo annuntiabatur: Zradidi enim, inquit, vobis in primis, quoniam Christus mortuus est pro peccatis nostris secundum Scripturas, et quoniam sepultus est, et resurrewit tertia die secwndum Scripturas. 3. Manifestum est igitur, quoniam Paulus alterum Christum nescit, nisi hune solum, qui et passus est, et sepultus est, et resurrexit, qui et natus est, quem et hominem dixit. Cum enim dixisset: Si autem Christus annuntiatur quoniam a mortuis resurrexit, intulit, rationem reddens incarnationis ejus: Quoniam per hominem mors, et per hominem resurrectio mortuorum. Et ubique in passione Domini nostri, et humanitate, et mortificatione ejus, Christi usus est nomine, quemadmodum in illo: Noli esca tua perdere illum, pro quo Christus mortuus est. Et iterum: Nune autem in Christo vos qui aliquando fuistis longe, facti estis proximi in sanguine Christi. Et iterum: Christus nos redemit de maledicto Legis, factus pro nobis maledictum: quoniam scriptum est, Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno. Et iterum: Et periet infirmus in tua scientia frater, propter quem Ohristus mortuus est; significans, quoniam non Christus impassibilis descendit in Jesum, sed ipse, Jesus Christus cum esset, passus est pro nobis, qui decubuit et resurrexit, qui descendit et ascendit, Filius Dei, filius hominis factus: quemadmodum et ipsum nomen significat. In Christi enim nomine subauditur qui unxit, et ipse qui unctus est, et ipsa unctio in qua unctus est. Et unxit quidem Pater, unctus est vero Filius, in Spiritu, qui est unctio; quemadmodum per Esaiam ait sermo: Spiritus Dei super me, propter quod unwit me; significans et unguentem Patrem, et unctum Filium, et unctionem, qui est Spiritus. 4. Et ipse autem Dominus manifestum facit eum qui est passus. Cum enim interrogasset discipulos: Quem me homines dicunt esse Filium Hominis? ®et Petrus cum respondisset: Ju es Christus Filius Dei vivi; et cum laudatus esset ab eo, Quoniam caro et sanguis non revelavit ei, sed Pater qui est in coelis, manifestum fecit, quoniam Filius Hominis hie est Christus Filius Dei vivi: He eo enim, inquit, capit demonstrare discentibus, quoniam oportet illum Hierosolymam ire, et multa pati a sacerdotibus, 1 et reprobari, et crucifigi, et tertia die resurgere. Ipse qui agnitus est a Petro Christus, qui eum beatum dixit, quoniam Pater ei revelavit Filium Dei vivi, dixit, semetipsum oportere multa pati et crucifigi: et tune Petro increpavit, secundum opinionem hominum putanti eum esse Christum, et passionem ejus ayersanti, et dixit discipulis: Si gwis eult post me venire, neget se, et tollat crucom suam, et sequatur me. Qui enim voluerit animam suam salvare, perdet illam: et qui eam perdiderit propter me, salvabit eam. Hee enim Christus manifeste dicebat, ipse exsistens Salvator eorum, qui propter suam confessionem in mortem traderentur, et perderent animas suas. Si autem ipse non erat passurus, sed Savolaret a Jesu, quid et adhortabatur discipulos tollere erucem, et sequi se, quam ipse non tollebat secundum ipsos, sed relinquebat dispositionem passionis? Quoniam enim non de agnitione superioris crucis dicit hoc, quemadmodum quidam audent exponere; sed de passione, quam oportebat illum pati, et ipsi discipuli ejus futurum erat ut paterentur, intulit: Quicungue enim salvaverit animam suam, perdet cam: et qui perdiderit, inveniet eam; et quoniam passuri erant discipuli ejus propter eum, dicebat Judzis: Hece, ego mitto ad vos prophetas, et sapientes, et doctores, et ex his interficietis, et crucifigetis; et discipulis dicebat, Ante duces et reges stabitis propter me, et ex vobis flagellabunt, et interficient, et persequentur a civitate in civitatem; sciebat igitur et eos qui persecutionem passuri essent, sciebat et eos qui flagellari et occidi haberent propter eum: et non altera de cruce, sed de passione, quam passurus esset ipse prior, post deinde discipuli ejus. Erat ergo sermo ejus adhortans etiam illos: WVolite timere eos qui occidunt corpus, animam autem non possunt occidere: timete autem magis eum, qui habet potestatem et corpus et animam mittere in gehennam; et servare eas quze essent ad eum confessiones. Etenim ipse confessurum se promittebat coram Patre eos qui confiterentur nomen suum coram hominibus; negaturum autem eos qui negarent eum, et confusurum qui confunderentur confessionem ejus. Et cum hee ita se habeant, ad tantam temeritatem progressi sunt quidam, ut etiam martyres spernant, et vituperent eos qui propter Domini confessionem occiduntur, et sustinent omnia a Domino preedicta, et secundum hoc conantur vestigia assequi passionis Domini, passibilis martyres facti; quos et concedimus ipsis martyribus. Cum enim inquiretur sanguis eorum, et gloriam consequentur, tune a Christo confundentur omnes qui inhonoraverunt eorum martyrium. 5. Et ex hoc autem quod Dominus in cruce dixerit : Pater eis, non enim sciunt quid faciunt, longanimitas, et patientia, et misericordia, et bonitas Christi ostenditur, ut et ipse pateretur, et ipse excusaret eos qui se male " tractassent. Verbum enim Dei quod nobis dixit: Diligite inimicos vestros, et orate pro eis qui vos oderunt, ipse hoe fecit in cruce, in tantum diligens humanum genus, ut etiam pro his qui se interficerent, postularet. Si quis autem quasi duorum exsistentium, judicium de his faciat, invenietur multo melior, et patientior, et vere bonus, qui in vulneribus ipsis, et plagis, et reliquis que in eum commiserunt, beneficus est, nec memor est in se commissze malitize, eo qui avolavit, nec ullam injuriam, neque opprobrium passus est. Hoc autem idem et illis occurrit, qui dicunt eum putative passum. Si enim non vere passus est, nulla gratia ei, cum nulla fuerit passio: et nos, cum incipiemus vere pati, seducens videbitur, adhortans nos yapulare, et alteram preebere maxillam, si ipse illud non prior in veritate passus est: et quemadmodum illos seduxit, ut videretur eis ipse hoc quod non erat, et nos seducit, adhortans perferre ea, quze ipse non pertulit. Erimus autem et super magistrum, dum patimur et sustinemus quze neque passus est neque sustinuit magister. Sed quoniam solus vere magister Dominus noster, et bonus vere Filius Dei et patiens, Verbum Dei Patris Filius Hominis factus. Luctatus est enim, et vicit : erat enim homo ' pro patribus certans, et per obedientiam, inobedientiam persolvens: alligavit enim fortem, et solvit infirmos, et salutem donavit plasmati suo, destruens peccatum. Est enim piissimus et misericors Dominus, et amans humanum genus. re, et py at te? wn 6. Heerere itaque fecit et adunivit, quemadmodum preediximus, hominem Deo. Si enim homo non vicisset inimicum hominis, non juste victus esset inimicus. Rursus autem nisi Deus donasset salutem, non firmiter haberemus eam. Et nisi homo ®conjunctus fuisset Deo, non potuisset particeps fieri incorruptibilitatis. Oportuerat enim Mediatorem Dei et hominum, per suam ad utrosque domesticitatem, in amicitiam et concordiam utrosque reducere, let facere, ut et Deus assumeret hominem, et homo se dederet Deo. Qua enim ratione filiorum adoptionis ejus participes esse possemus, nisi per Filium eam que est ad ipsum recepissemus ab eo communionem, nisi verbum ejus communicasset nobis caro factum ? Quapropter et per omnem venit zetatem, omnibus restituens eam quze est ad Deum communionem. Igitur qui dicunt eum putative manifestatum, neque in carne natum, neque vere hominem factum, adhuc sub veteri sunt damnatione, advocationem preebentes. peccato, non devicta secundum eos morte, que regnavit ab Adam usque ad Moysem, etiam in eos qui non peccaverunt in similitudinem transgressionis Adw. Veniens autem lex, que data est per Moysem, et testificans de peccato, quoniam peccator est, regnum quidem ejus abstulit, latronem et non regem eum detegens, et homicidam eum ostendit : oneravit autem hominem qui habebat peccatum in se, reum mortis ostendens eum, Spiritalis enim cum lex esset, manifestavit tantummodo peccatum, non autem interemit: non enim Spiritui dominabatur peccatum, sed homini, Oportebat enim eum qui inciperet occidere peccatum, et mortis reum redimere hominem, id ipsum fieri quod erat ille, id est hominem: qui a peccato quidem in servitium tractus fuerat, a morte vero tenebatur, ut peccatum ab homine interficeretur, et homo exiret a morte. Quemadmodum enim per inobedientiam unius hominis, qui primus de terra rudi plasmatus est, peccatores facti sunt multi, et amiserunt vitam; ita oportuit et per obedientiam unius hominis, qui primus ex virgine natus est, justificari multos, et percipere salutem. Sic igitur Verbum Dei homo factus est, quemadmodum et Moyses ait: Deus, vera opera ejus. Si autem non factus caro parebat quasi caro, non erat verum opus ejus. Quod autem parebat, hoe et erat; Deus, hominis antiquam plasmationem in se recapitulans, ut occideret quidem peccatum, evacuaret autem mortem, et vivificaret hominem: et propter hoc vera opera ejus.
thought_title: The Word of God Became Human
pass_a_gloss: It is shown clearly, that the Word of God, existing in the beginning with God, through whom all things were made, who also always was present with the human race, this one in the last times according to the predetermined time from the Father, united with his own creation, made a passible human, excluded is all contradiction of those saying: If therefore he was born then, he was not before Christ. For we show, that the Son of God did not begin then, existing always with the Father; but when he was made flesh, and made human, he recapitulated in himself the long exposition of humans, providing in brief salvation to us, so that what we lost in Adam, that is, to be according to the image and likeness of God, this we might receive in Christ Jesus. For it was not possible for the human who once was conquered and defeated through disobedience to be remade, and to obtain salvation by victory, and again it was impossible for him to receive salvation who fell under sin, both things the Son, the Word of God existing, descending from the Father, and made flesh, and descending to death, and completing the dispensation of our salvation, to which we are undoubtedly exhorted to believe, saying again: Do not say in your heart, Who ascends into heaven? that is, to bring Christ down. Or, Who descends into the abyss? that is, to bring Christ up from the dead; then he adds: For if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved. And he gave the reason for which cause the Word of God did these things, saying: For in this Christ both lived, and died, and rose again, to be Lord of the living and the dead. And again writing to the Corinthians he says: For we preach Christ Jesus crucified. And he adds: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? Who is it that has communion with us in foods? Is it he who is said to be Christ, extended above, that is, to the end, and formed their mother? Or is it he who is from the virgin, Emmanuel, who ate butter and honey, about whom the prophet says: And he is human, and who knows him? This same one was preached by Paul: For I delivered to you in the first place, that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, and that he was buried, and rose again on the third day according to the Scriptures. It is clear therefore, that Paul knows no other Christ, except this one, who suffered, and was buried, and rose again, who also was born, and whom he called human. For when he said: If Christ is preached as risen from the dead, he introduced, giving the reason for his incarnation: For through a human death, and through a human resurrection of the dead. And everywhere in the passion of our Lord, and his humanity, and his death, the name of Christ is used, just as in that: Do not lose the one for whom Christ died. And again: Now you who once were far off have been made near in the blood of Christ. And again: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law, having become a curse for us, for it is written: Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree. And again: And the weak brother for whom Christ died will be lost in your knowledge; showing that it was not the impassible Christ who descended into Jesus, but Jesus Christ himself, who being human, suffered for us, who lay down and rose again, who descended and ascended, the Son of God, made human; just as the name itself signifies. For in the name of Christ is implied the one who anointed, and the one who was anointed, and the anointing in which he was anointed. And the Father anointed, the Son was anointed, in the Spirit, who is the anointing; just as the word says through Isaiah: The Spirit of God is upon me, because he anointed me; showing the anointing Father, and the anointed Son, and the anointing, which is the Spirit. And the Lord himself makes clear the one who suffered. For when he asked the disciples: Who do humans say the Son of Man is? and Peter responded: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God; and when he was praised by him, because flesh and blood did not reveal it to him, but the Father who is in heaven, he made clear that the Son of Man is this Christ, the Son of the living God: For he said, demonstrating to the disciples, that it is necessary for him to go to Jerusalem, and to suffer many things from the priests, and to be rejected, and to be crucified, and to rise again on the third day. He himself, who was recognized by Peter as Christ, who called him blessed, because the Father revealed to him the Son of the living God, said that it was necessary for him to suffer many things and to be crucified; and then he rebuked Peter, thinking according to human opinion that he was Christ, and denying his passion, and said to the disciples: If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whoever wants to save his soul will lose it, and whoever loses it for my sake will save it. For Christ clearly said these things, being himself the Savior of those who would be handed over to death for his sake, and would lose their souls. But if he himself was not going to suffer, but to be saved by Jesus, why did he exhort the disciples to take up the cross and follow him, which he himself did not take up according to them, but left the disposition of the passion? For he did not speak of the knowledge of the superior cross, as some dare to explain; but of the passion, which it was necessary for him to suffer, and for his disciples to suffer in the future, he introduced: For whoever saves his soul will lose it, and whoever loses it will find it; and because his disciples would suffer for his sake, he said to the Jews: Behold, I send to you prophets, and wise men, and teachers, and you will kill and crucify some of them; and to the disciples he said, You will stand before governors and kings for my sake, and they will flog you, and kill you, and persecute you from city to city; therefore he knew both those who would suffer persecution, and those who would be flogged and killed for his sake; and not of another cross, but of the passion, which he himself would suffer first, and then his disciples. His word was therefore an exhortation to them also: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul; but fear him who has the power to throw both body and soul into hell; and to keep those who make confessions to him. For he himself promised to confess before the Father those who would confess his name before humans; but to deny those who would deny him, and to confound those who would confound his confession. And when these things are so, some have progressed to such temerity, that they even despise martyrs, and reproach those who are killed for the confession of the Lord, and endure all things predicted by the Lord, and according to this try to follow the footsteps of the passion of the Lord, having become passible martyrs; whom we also concede to the martyrs. For when their blood is required, and they attain glory, then all those who dishonored their martyrdom will be confounded by Christ. And from the fact that the Lord said on the cross: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do, the long-suffering, and patience, and mercy, and goodness of Christ are shown, so that he himself suffered, and he himself excused those who treated him badly. For the Word of God, who said to us: Love your enemies, and pray for those who hate you, did this on the cross, loving the human race so much, that he even prayed for those who killed him. If anyone makes a judgment about these things, as if there were two existing, he will find that the one who is good, and patient, and truly good, is the one who is beneficial in the wounds, and blows, and other things that were done to him, and does not remember the evil done to him; whereas the other did not suffer any injury, or reproach. This same thing happens to those who say that he suffered apparently. For if he did not truly suffer, there is no grace to him, since there was no passion; and we, when we begin to truly suffer, will seem to be deceived, being exhorted to endure, and to offer the other cheek, if he himself did not first suffer truly. And just as he deceived them, so that it seemed to them that he was what he was not, so he deceives us, exhorting us to endure things that he himself did not endure. We will be above the master, while we suffer and endure things that the master did not suffer or endure. But since our Lord is the only true master, and the truly good Son of God, and patient, the Word of God made human; for he struggled, and conquered; he was human, fighting for the fathers, and paying the debt of disobedience through obedience; he bound the strong one, and freed the weak, and gave salvation to his creation, destroying sin. For he is the most pious, and merciful Lord, and loving the human race. He therefore did and united, as we have said, the human with God. For if the human had not conquered the enemy of humans, the enemy would not have been justly conquered. Again, unless God had given salvation, we would not have it firmly. And unless the human had been joined to God, he could not have become a partaker of incorruptibility. For it was necessary for a mediator between God and humans, through his domesticity with both, to lead both into friendship and harmony, and to make it so that God would take up the human, and the human would give himself to God. For how could we have become partakers of the adoption of sons, unless we had received from him the communion that is with him, unless his Word had become flesh and communicated with us? Therefore, he came through every age, restoring to all the communion that is with God. Therefore, those who say that he appeared apparently, and was not born in the flesh, and was not truly made human, are still under the old condemnation, offering an advocacy for sin, not conquered by death, which reigned from Adam to Moses, even in those who did not sin in the likeness of the transgression of Adam. But when the law came, which was given through Moses, and testified to sin, that the sinner is, it took away his kingdom, showing him to be a thief and not a king, and showing him to be a murderer; but it burdened the human who had sin in himself, showing him to be guilty of death; for the law was spiritual, and it showed sin, but did not destroy it; for sin did not dominate the Spirit, but the human. It was necessary therefore for the one who would begin to kill sin, and redeem the human who was guilty of death, to become what that human was, that is, human; who had been led into servitude by sin, and was held by death, so that sin might be killed by the human, and the human might exit from death. For just as through the disobedience of one human, who was first formed from the earth, many became sinners, and lost life; so it was necessary that through the obedience of one human, who was first born from the virgin, many would be justified, and receive salvation. Therefore, the Word of God became human, just as Moses also says: God, true are his works. But if he had not been made flesh, he would not have been a true work; what he appeared to be, that he also was; God, recapitulating in himself the ancient formation of the human, so that he might kill sin, and destroy death, and vivify the human; and for this reason, his works are true.

His word was therefore an exhortation to them also: Do not be afraid of those who kill the body, but cannot kill the soul; but fear him who has the power to throw both body and soul into hell; and to keep those who make confessions to him. For he himself promised to confess before the Father those who would confess his name before humans; but to deny those who would deny him, and to confound those who would confound his confession. And when these things are so, some have progressed to such temerity, that they even despise martyrs, and reproach those who are killed for the confession of the Lord, and endure all things predicted by the Lord, and according to this try to follow the footsteps of the passion of the Lord, having become passible martyrs; whom we also concede to the martyrs. For when their blood is required, and they attain glory, then all those who dishonored their martyrdom will be confounded by Christ. And from the fact that the Lord said on the cross: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do, the long-suffering, and patience, and mercy, and goodness of Christ are shown, so that he himself suffered, and he himself excused those who treated him badly. For the Word of God, who said to us: Love your enemies, and pray for those who hate you, did this on the cross, loving the human race so much, that he even prayed for those who killed him. If anyone makes a judgment about these things, as if there were two existing, he will find that the one who is good, and patient, and truly good, is the one who is beneficial in the wounds, and blows, and other things that were done to him, and does not remember the evil done to him; whereas the other did not suffer any injury, or reproach. This same thing happens to those who say that he suffered apparently. For if he did not truly suffer, there is no grace to him, since there was no passion; and we, when we begin to truly suffer, will seem to be deceived, being exhorted to endure, and to offer the other cheek, if he himself did not first suffer truly. And just as he deceived them, so that it seemed to them that he was what he was not, so he deceives us, exhorting us to endure things that he himself did not endure. We will be above the master, while we suffer and endure things that the master did not suffer or endure. But since our Lord is the only true master, and the truly good Son of God, and patient, the Word of God made human; for he struggled, and conquered; he was human, fighting for the fathers, and paying the debt of disobedience through obedience; he bound the strong one, and freed the weak, and gave salvation to his creation, destroying sin. For he is the most pious, and merciful Lord, and loving the human race. He therefore did and united, as we have said, the human with God. For if the human had not conquered the enemy of humans, the enemy would not have been justly conquered. Again, unless God had given salvation, we would not have it firmly. And unless the human had been joined to God, he could not have become a partaker of incorruptibility. For it was necessary for a mediator between God and humans, through his domesticity with both, to lead both into friendship and harmony, and to make it so that God would take up the human, and the human would give himself to God. For how could we have become partakers of the adoption of sons, unless we had received from him the communion that is with him, unless his Word had become flesh and communicated with us? Therefore, he came through every age, restoring to all the communion that is with God. Therefore, those who say that he appeared apparently, and was not born in the flesh, and was not truly made human, are still under the old condemnation, offering an advocacy for sin, not conquered by death, which reigned from Adam to Moses, even in those who did not sin in the likeness of the transgression of Adam. But when the law came, which was given through Moses, and testified to sin, that the sinner is, it took away his kingdom, showing him to be a thief and not a king, and showing him to be a murderer; but it burdened the human who had sin in himself, showing him to be guilty of death; for the law was spiritual, and it showed sin, but did not destroy it; for sin did not dominate the Spirit, but the human. It was necessary therefore for the one who would begin to kill sin, and redeem the human who was guilty of death, to become what that human was, that is, human; who had been led into servitude by sin, and was held by death, so that sin might be killed by the human, and the human might exit from death. For just as through the disobedience of one human, who was first formed from the earth, many became sinners, and lost life; so it was necessary that through the obedience of one human, who was first born from the virgin, many would be justified, and receive salvation. Therefore, the Word of God became human, just as Moses also says: God, true are his works. But if he had not been made flesh, he would not have been a true work; what he appeared to be, that he also was; God, recapitulating in himself the ancient formation of the human, so that he might kill sin, and destroy death, and vivify the human; and for this reason, his works are true (Isaiah 61:1).
